newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says Iran gas pipeline to start March-April.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says Iran gas pipeline to start March-April.

text.p: Construction of a natural gas pipeline between Iran and Turkey will begin in late March or early April, the Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan said on Wednesday.
He also said work was continuing on increasing natural gas imports from Russia and Algeria to meet growing domestic demand.
"I hope that at the end of March or the start of April the construction will start with a ceremony on the Turkish-Iranian border," Kutan said in a speech at a ceremony in Ankara.
The two countries signed a $23-billion, 23-year gas deal last August.
The pipeline will carry an initial four billion cubic metres of Iranian gas annually, to be raised in subsequent years to 10 billion cubic metres a year, Kutan said.

Turkish state-owned pipeline company Botas last December sought bids for construction of a 300-km (188-mile) stretch of the pipeline from the eastern Turkish towns of Erzurum and Dogubeyazit on the Iranian border.
From Erzurum the gas will be connected by pipeline with the Turkish capital Ankara.
Iran will build a 270-km (169-mile) pipeline from the town of Tabriz to the Turkish border.
Kutan also said talks with Russian officials on raising natural gas imports from Russia to 16 billion cubic metres annually from six billion had reached their final stage.
Natural gas imports from Algeria would be increased to four billion cubic metres from two billion currently, he said.
Turkish energy demand is expected to rise around 12 percent annually in the coming years.
Kutan said 55 percent of the natural gas imports would be used in generating electricity.
